nodes.label: Fidere BaaS Interlace PRD App
nodes.rationale: The package is a private Vite React product-manual application for Fidere BaaS / Interlace PRD work.

nodes.label: Tailwind Design Token Theme
nodes.rationale: Theme colors and radii are mapped to CSS variables so UI primitives can share a consistent design-token layer.

nodes.label: Client-side Path Router
nodes.rationale: Routing is implemented against window.location and history state instead of a router package, keeping the PRD prototype lightweight.

nodes.label: Header Product Positioning
nodes.rationale: The header states that Fidere Trust is customer-facing while Interlace / BaaS is the lower-level execution tool, and that the page uses local demo data only.

nodes.label: Investment Product PRD
nodes.rationale: Unifies development, testing, product, and admin understanding of first-version fixed-income rules without expanding API, database, or interface field design.

nodes.label: Fixed Income MVP Rule Set
nodes.rationale: First version focuses on clear rules, reconcilable amounts, auditable operations, retestable behavior, and controlled development complexity instead of a complex financial product engine.

nodes.label: Fixed Income Subscription to Settlement Flow
nodes.norm_label: fixed income subscription to settlement flow

nodes.label: Versioned Yield Rates
nodes.rationale: Directly overwriting rates would miscalculate historical orders; retaining effective-dated versions supports audit, reconciliation, and customer explanation.

nodes.label: Independent Position Lot
nodes.rationale: Independent lots keep each fund tranche's value date, maturity date, rate version, and calculation interval separate, making reconciliation, tracing, and customer explanation simpler.

nodes.label: Special Early Exit
nodes.rationale: MVP avoids automatic redemption because fixed-term products discourage early exit, external exit costs may be uncertain, and automatic calculations are dispute-prone.

nodes.label: Natural-Day Maturity Schedule
nodes.rationale: Natural-day rules are simple, stable, and easier for development, testing, admins, and users to understand; market holiday handling is deferred.

nodes.label: Admin Permission Boundary
nodes.rationale: The first version uses one administrator role for all backend operations; operations, finance, compliance, and reviewer roles are deferred.

nodes.label: First Phase MVP Scope
nodes.rationale: First phase prioritizes stable, clear, testable, and reconcilable fixed-income behavior over building all advanced financial engine features.

nodes.label: Phase 2 IPO Subscription Allocation Refund Flow
nodes.rationale: IPO is excluded from the MVP fixed-income mainline and retained as second-phase development scope.
nodes.norm_label: phase 2 ipo subscription allocation refund flow

nodes.label: Manual IPO Final Profit Confirmation
nodes.rationale: IPO final profit is not auto-calculated because subscription amount, allocation, exit time, exit price, fees, financing costs, and special arrangements vary by user.

nodes.label: PRD Local Comment Board
nodes.rationale: First version deliberately skips permissions, required fields, and format validation to support lightweight PRD questions, conclusions, and change suggestions directly on the page.

nodes.label: BaaS Interlace PRD Context
nodes.rationale: The manual is explicitly local demo data only: no real APIs, no real Interlace integration, and no database writes.

nodes.label: PRD Portal Module Catalog
nodes.rationale: Centralizes PRD, legacy investment PRD, and BaaS prototype entries so the portal can route product manuals and prototypes from one catalog.

nodes.label: PRD Invest Legacy Sections
nodes.rationale: Keeps legacy fixed-income PRD rules available inside the current product manual portal without merging them into the BaaS PRD.

nodes.label: Product Manual Module Search and Filter
nodes.norm_label: product manual module search and filter

nodes.label: Transfer Balance Impact Model
nodes.rationale: Separates client-visible balances from Interlace actual balance and internal funding records to preserve the product boundary.

nodes.label: US Account Client Prototype State Machine
nodes.norm_label: us account client prototype state machine

nodes.label: US Account Visibility Gate
nodes.rationale: The prototype hides US account actions and bank account details until the simulated account status permits them.

nodes.label: Enterprise KYB Supplement Flow
nodes.rationale: Groups enterprise base, shareholder, and director fields to keep missing documents and format-conversion issues attached to the responsible entity.

nodes.label: BaaS PRD Product Boundary
nodes.rationale: Fidere Trust is positioned as relationship, instruction, fee, review, and internal ledger layer, while Interlace/BaaS remains the underlying execution tool.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Manual Execution
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 intentionally keeps account opening, payee, payout, USDT funding, and OTC as Admin-driven operations before later automation.

nodes.label: Client Available Balance Rule
nodes.rationale: Customers should see Fidere-calculated available and pending balances, not raw Interlace actual balance or internal execution costs.

nodes.label: Fidere Beneficiary Boundary
nodes.rationale: Clients maintain and choose Fidere Beneficiary records, while BaaS Payee identifiers remain Admin-only execution data.

nodes.label: BaaS Prototype Review Reference
nodes.rationale: The prototype document decomposes the main PRD into reviewable wireframes for visibility, manual execution nodes, and acceptance checks.
